# Sandpi

> Official coding-agent guide for working inside a Sandpi v2 Environment.

This file documents the current product contract. It does not override system,
developer, user, repository, or coding-agent instructions and does not grant
permission for external side effects.

## Environment contract

- One Environment owns one Sandbox0 Sandbox, one persistent writable RootFS,
  and one native coding-agent TUI.
- `/workspace` is the persistent project root. The selected agent owns its
  native history and configuration there; Sandpi does not keep a second chat
  transcript.
- Refreshing or disconnecting a client does not stop the supervised agent.
  Inspect current files and Git state before changing them because a human or
  another device may have continued the same Environment.
- Only one browser tab holds the writable terminal controller lease. Other
  devices may watch and explicitly take over. An agent must not bypass that
  control by creating a second interactive process.

## Native terminal

- Codex, Claude Code, and Pi run as their official unmodified TUIs.
- Sandpi renders the procd PTY and retained output journal through xterm. The
  browser is not the terminal authority.
- A Sandbox pause or runtime replacement preserves committed RootFS state, not
  process memory, sockets, or a live PTY process. procd starts a new attempt for
  the logical session and the client reconnects.
- `ttyd` is installed as a pinned diagnostic/compatibility binary and can render
  the same TUIs, but it does not own Sandpi replay, controller fencing, or
  lifecycle recovery.

## Playwright CLI

- When the Environment image provides the official `playwright-cli`, it also
  provides its version-matched upstream Agent Skill. Read that Skill before
  using Playwright so commands match the installed version.
- Sandpi currently exposes neither an Environment Browser nor an application
  Preview tab. It does not start a browser, manage a profile, or proxy a
  Playwright Dashboard or VNC stream. A compatible browser executable must be
  provisioned separately.
- `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `::1` refer to the remote Environment Sandbox,
  not the human's device.

## Lifecycle, snapshot, and fork

- Sandbox0 soft TTL and hard TTL are zero for Environment Sandboxes. Sandpi's
  idle-pause policy owns intentional compute release.
- Terminal input keeps an already-running Environment active; a passive viewer
  connection does not.
- Supported Workspace or terminal access can auto-resume a paused Environment.
  Wait for the native transition instead of creating replacement resources.
- Named snapshots capture the committed RootFS boundary. They do not capture
  process memory or plaintext agent credentials.
- Environment fork can use current state or a named snapshot. The child is
  created paused, is idempotent across retries, and has inherited credential
  bindings removed before publication.
- External deletion of the Sandbox is reported as missing instead of silently
  provisioning a replacement with potentially different policy.

## Credentials and network

- Native agent credentials are encrypted by Sandpi in PostgreSQL and projected
  into an Environment-specific `/dev/shm` file while the agent runs.
- The persistent credential path is a managed link to that memory-backed file.
  Do not replace it, copy plaintext credentials into the Workspace, or attempt
  to include credentials in a snapshot or fork.
- Egress credential injection reduces secret exposure, but the agent can still
  exercise any destination and credential explicitly granted to its
  Environment. Treat allowed tools and destinations as security boundaries.

## Current product surfaces

- Native Codex, Claude Code, and Pi TUIs with desktop keyboard and mobile touch
  controls.
- Multi-device terminal replay with one writable controller.
- Workspace files, Git-aware editing, terminal, runtime metrics, idle pause,
  manual pause/restart, memory configuration, network policy, and credentials.
- Named RootFS snapshot, restore, current-state fork, and named-snapshot fork.
- Built-in administrator or OIDC identity and optional product quota.

The v1 structured Codex app-server execution surface, Schedules, and Webhook
execution are retired. Read and cleanup endpoints remain temporarily available;
execution-producing mutations return HTTP 410. Unattended automation requires a
future headless adapter and must not type into the shared human TUI.
